lines.trans: 'Esteemed municipal representative, for over eighty years this historic courtyard...'
Boss, if you talk like a tax textbook, the clerk will fall asleep standing up.
Take one deep breath, Mazen, and put all five pages in the drawer.
In the drawer?! Then what do I say when they walk through the gate?!
Say 'Good afternoon, welcome to Room Nine, please sit down for hot tea!'
Let the sunlit glass, Salma's warm bread, and Suad's piano do the talking.
You really think simple hospitality is enough?
Hospitality is what this house has done best for over eighty years, Mazen.
Wait—are my reading glasses on my forehead right now?
Safely in your jacket pocket, boss. Tie straight, shoes clean.
Listen—the courtyard gate bell just rang! Three o'clock on the dot!

meanings.note: Formal honorific title meaning 'Your/Esteemed Presence', used in official speeches.

examples.trans: We used the word حضرة.
This is another حضرة.

meanings.note: Agent noun from مثّل (to represent), meaning a delegate or representative.

examples.trans: We used the word ممثّل.
This is another ممثّل.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بلديات.

examples.trans: He works in the contracts office at the municipality.
The municipal building is next to the square.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: محترمة, plural: محترمين).

examples.trans: His voice is calm and very polite.
A respectable, well-known family in the quarter.

meanings.note: Literary/MSA preposition for 'since/for', highlighting Mazen's overly stiff speech.

examples.trans: We used the word منذ.
This is another منذ.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of أكثر ('more, most').

examples.trans: I liked working here much more.
Who knows the neighbourhood better than you?

meanings.note: Everyday preposition meaning 'from', 'of', or 'than' after comparatives.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eighty'.

examples.text: خشب بلوط أصلي عمره تمانين سنة.
examples.trans: Solid oak wood eighty years old.
This house has lived through eighty winters!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سنين.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.

meanings.note: MSA feminine demonstrative used in Mazen's stiff written draft.

examples.trans: We used the word هذه.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساحات.

examples.trans: The courtyard has a big jasmine tree.

meanings.note: Nisba adjective from تاريخ (history), agreeing with الساحة.

examples.trans: We used the word تاريخي.
This is another تاريخي.

meanings.note: In Jordanian speech, يا معلم is an affectionate, respectful way to address a boss or skilled craftsperson.

examples.trans: You are all generosity, boss!
She was a very gifted piano teacher.

meanings.note: Everyday conditional word 'if' for real possibilities.

examples.text: رني الجرس إذا احتجتي أي شي.
examples.trans: Ring the bell if you need anything.

examples.text: إذا فتحنا الساحة الصبح، الجيران بيفرحوا.
examples.trans: If we open the courtyard in the morning, the neighbours will be delighted.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to speak, talk, tell' (بحكي / حكى).

examples.trans: Salma chats with all the neighbours.
Tell me everything I need to know.

meanings.note: Spoken word for 'like': زيك 'like you'; زي ما 'just as, the way that'.

examples.trans: I want a glass of tea like yesterday.
Do it the way I taught you.

meanings.note: Masculine noun; plural كتب (kutub), written like the verb كتب 'he wrote' (katab) but said differently.

examples.trans: This book is about the history of Amman.
I put the books on the shelf.

meanings.note: Spoken plural of ضريبة (tax).

examples.trans: We used the word ضريبة.
This is another ضريبة.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: موظفين.

examples.trans: I am the new receptionist at the guesthouse.
All the staff here are helpful and friendly.

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Levantine future marker placed before a subjunctive verb (without ب-).

examples.text: ضيفة غرفة أربعة رح تقعد كل الأسبوع.
examples.trans: Room four's guest will stay all week.

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day is not going to be boring!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنام, بينام).

examples.trans: I feel I will sleep well tonight.
Did you sleep well under the wooden ceiling?

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'he' or 'it' (masculine).

examples.trans: He knows heritage law well.

examples.text: بيحكي هيك وهو بيطل من الشباك!
examples.trans: He says that while peeking out the window!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: واقفة, plural: واقفين).

examples.trans: There is nobody standing in the courtyard.
They stood face to face under the tree.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Unvocalised نفس covers nafas ('breath': خد نفس عميق take a deep breath) and nafs ('same': نفس الشي the same thing).

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
We took the exact same bus in the morning.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: عميقة, plural: عميقين).

examples.trans: Take a deep breath and calm down.
The old well is very deep.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a name or title when addressing someone in Arabic (يا نور 'Nour!', يا أستاذ 'sir!') and in exclamations (يا سلام! 'wonderful!').

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Male given name of the guesthouse owner.

examples.trans: We used the word مازن.
This is another مازن.

meanings.note: Everyday Levantine verb حطّ ('to put/place').

examples.trans: We used the word حطّ.

meanings.note: Numeral 'five'; short form خمس (khams) before a plural noun (خمس دقايق 'five minutes').

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: One sheet of paper or one leaf; the collective ورق means paper in general.

examples.trans: Write your number down for me on a piece of paper.
The tree leaf turns yellow in autumn.

meanings.note: Before an indefinite singular noun كل means 'every' (كل يوم 'every day'); before a definite noun it means 'all / the whole' (كل الأسبوع 'all week').

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Unvocalised درج covers both daraj ('stairs', masculine collective) and durj ('desk drawer').

examples.trans: Go up the stairs to the second floor.
The big notebook is inside the drawer.

meanings.note: Classic Levantine discourse word meaning 'then / well then / in that case'.

examples.trans: We used the word لكان.
This is another لكان.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine question word for 'what?'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian conjunction 'when' (in statements, not questions).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: The Levantine everyday verb for entering a room or building (فوت! 'come in!'), where formal Arabic says دخل.

examples.trans: Come in, the door is open.
We went into the restaurant at eight.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: بوابات.

examples.trans: The courtyard gate is open for guests.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form مسا (masa) alongside standard مساء in مساء الخير ('good evening').

examples.trans: The eight o'clock evening bus is arriving.

meanings.note: Core word in صباح الخير ('good morning'), مساء الخير ('good evening'), تصبح على خير ('good night'), and rising-tone خير؟ ('is everything okay?').

examples.text: سهل نرتب الكراسي بعد ما يخلص الدهان.

meanings.en: to please come in / sit / go ahead / here you are
meanings.note: Essential Jordanian hospitality verb used mostly in the imperative: تفضل (to a man), تفضلي (to a woman), تفضلوا (plural).

examples.trans: Please have a seat, ma'am!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقعد, بيقعد).

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: دافية, plural: دافيين).

هم.gloss: to matter; worry (ولا يهمك never mind / do not worry)

meanings.en: to matter; worry (ولا يهمك never mind / do not worry)
meanings.note: Used especially in the warm Jordanian reassurance ولا يهمك! ('never mind! / do not worry at all!').

examples.trans: Do not worry at all, sir, it is nothing!

meanings.note: Invariant spoken Jordanian relative pronoun ('who, which, that') for any gender or number.

examples.trans: That is what I want.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.

examples.trans: My grandfather's workshop was on this street.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفكر, بيفكر).

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'she' or 'it' (feminine).

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian form of شيء; combines in كل شي ('everything'), أي شي ('anything'), ولا شي ('nothing').

في.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

meanings.en: there is; there are; is there?
meanings.note: Spoken Levantine existential word ('there is / there are'); negated as ما في ('there is no / there are no').

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قراءات.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'on, at, to'; before ال- it regularly contracts to عال- ('al- / 'a-).

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجبنة.

meanings.note: Core Jordanian adjective meaning 'right, straight, accurate, on point'.

examples.trans: We used the word مزبوط.

meanings.note: Classic Levantine word for dress shoes (pair of shoes, treated as feminine singular).

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ساعات.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'three'; short form تلات (talaat) directly before a plural noun (تلات سنين 'three years').

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: دقايق.

examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes on the dot.

meanings.note: From ابتسم (to smile); everyday noun for a warm smile.

meanings.note: Ubiquitous Jordanian/Levantine encourager ('come on! / let us...!').

examples.trans: Come on, let us bring the bag down into the light!
Let us go check out the room right now!

meanings.en: to go; be gone (راحت علينا we missed our chance)

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ضيوف.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قريبة, plural: قراب).

examples.text: علمت بيانو ببيت قريب من هون.
